svg.title: What each party receives
svg.desc: The run happens in one of two places: the operator's Windows desktop, or an ephemeral GitHub-hosted Ubuntu machine in the operator's private deployment repository. Kokoro, FFmpeg, ReportLab and PyMuPDF operate inside whichever runtime is selected, so an unattended run is not a machine-only path: selected newsletter text, article evidence, prompts, drafts, the MP3, the PDF, the transcript and temporary credential copies exist on the GitHub-hosted machine while the job runs. Gmail is granted the mailbox-wide read-only scope although application code queries only the configured label and date. Public websites receive ordinary HTTPS requests without newsletter login cookies, though normal connection metadata remains visible to them. Antigravity receives selected newsletter, article and daily-research evidence plus editorial instructions, and disabling telemetry does not make its inference offline. GitHub keeps Actions secrets encrypted in the private repository until they are rotated or deleted; temporary runner files are removed and no Actions artifact is uploaded, but GitHub retains workflow logs according to repository settings. Firebase Hosting receives the web app shell, RSS, MP3, PDF, artwork and public source links. Owner-locked Firestore receives generation and schedule parameters, queue, execution and runner state, episode metadata, source counts, up to one hundred references and up to five hundred timed transcript segments containing spoken editorial content, but not raw Gmail bodies, OAuth credentials, Gmail message identifiers, Antigravity request files, local paths or detailed local exceptions. The Cloudflare Durable Object stores schedule timing and opaque identifiers, while the Worker environment separately holds a scoped expiring GitHub dispatch token and transiently receives a short-lived Firebase identity token during authenticated synchronization; Cloudflare receives no newsletter text, Gmail credentials, episode media or editorial parameters. The podcast feed is a capability URL, so anyone holding it has access and it should be handled like a password, and Apple Podcasts or another client can retrieve and cache the feed and media.
svg.text: THE DAILY NEXUS
WHAT EACH PARTY RECEIVES
THE RUN HAPPENS IN ONE OF TWO PLACES
WINDOWS DESKTOP
The operator's own
computer.
GITHUB-HOSTED JOB
Ephemeral Ubuntu, private
repo.
NOT A MACHINE-ONLY PATH
Kokoro, FFmpeg, ReportLab and PyMuPDF run inside whichever
runtime is selected.
During an unattended run the selected newsletter text, article
evidence, prompts, drafts, the MP3, the PDF, the transcript and
temporary credential copies exist on the GitHub-hosted machine.
WHAT CROSSES TO EACH PARTY
GOOGLE GMAIL
Mailbox-wide read-only scope. Application code queries only the
configured label and date.
PUBLIC WEBSITES
Ordinary HTTPS requests, without newsletter login cookies.
Normal connection metadata is still visible to the site.
ANTIGRAVITY
Selected newsletter, article and daily-research evidence, plus
editorial instructions.
Telemetry off is not offline inference.
GITHUB
Actions secrets stay encrypted in the private repository until
rotated or deleted.
Temporary runner files are removed and no artifact is uploaded.
Workflow logs are retained per repository settings.
FIREBASE HOSTING
The web app shell, RSS, MP3, PDF, artwork and public source links.
FIRESTORE / OWNER-LOCKED
Generation and schedule parameters, queue, execution and
runner state, episode metadata and source counts.
Up to 100 references and up to 500 timed transcript segments.
The transcript holds spoken editorial content.
Not sent: raw Gmail bodies, OAuth credentials, Gmail message
IDs, Antigravity request files, local paths, detailed local
exceptions.
CLOUDFLARE
Durable Object: schedule timing and opaque IDs.
Worker environment: a scoped, expiring GitHub dispatch token,
and transiently a short-lived Firebase ID token during
authenticated sync.
Not sent: newsletter text, Gmail credentials, episode media,
editorial parameters.
APPLE PODCASTS / ANY CLIENT
The feed is a capability URL: whoever holds it has access, so
handle it like a password.
A client can fetch and cache the feed and media.
Revoking access happens at each provider. Deleting a file or a
repository does not revoke a grant.
